title: Marine Corps offers early exit to some enlisted troops
summary: Troops in 18 critical specialties can leave no earlier than 90 days before their contracts expire, rather than 180 days, because of “inventory shortfalls."

title: Army calls detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success after earlier fears of a toxic plume
summary: The U.S. Army has blown up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, because it had deteriorated and might explode uncontrollably. Officials say the first checks show no toxic dust spread to nearby homes and farms. The Army called Wednesday's detonation a success, with all 5 tons destroyed. The Environmental Protection Agency reported no lead in the air around the plant. Still, government agencies will do more testing in the coming days. Lead is a heavy metal that’s especially dangerous to children and pregnant women.

title: Pentagon hires conservative contractors to audit military base schools and pilot ‘classical’ PE
summary: The Defense Department continues to revamp its schools for military families to align with conservative education ideals. The Department of Defense Education Activity operates about 160 schools across 11 countries, educating children of service members. It has begun auditing curriculum and piloting what's called a "classical" physical education course at two U.S. campuses — in North Carolina and Virginia. The department awarded a $5.7 million contract to conservative-aligned American Education Solutions for a curriculum audit. A separate contract of around $100,000 was awarded to Iliad Athletics to start “classical” P.E., inspired by traditional Greek athletics. A Pentagon spokesperson says the agency regularly reviews its academic programs and makes improvements.

title: Army to detonate US stockpile of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa the day before Thanksgiving
summary: The U.S. Army says it plans to detonate the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning. It says waiting any longer raises the risks that the dangerously degrading bomb-making chemicals could explode at any time. Officials sought to assure residents that they’ve taken steps to put barriers around the blast zone and limit the plume from the detonation when it happens the day before Thanksgiving. Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said Tuesday there's no reason to panic. The controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown has set off concerns about potential health and environmental effects and frustration over a lack of information.
